collection.name: VERITAS AI demo reference collection
collection.description: Hand-built set of short, paraphrased summaries of widely established science and public-health facts, each linked to a public institutional page on the topic. The passages are written for this project; they are not verbatim quotations and were not reviewed line by line against each page, so always consult the linked source. Coverage is narrow (health, climate, space, earth science, physics, biology) and deliberately excludes contested political topics.

passages.passage: Vaccination protects against serious diseases such as measles, polio, diphtheria, tetanus and whooping cough. Immunization programmes prevent millions of deaths worldwide every year.

Antimicrobial resistance happens when bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites change over time and stop responding to medicines. Misuse and overuse of antimicrobials are the main drivers, which makes infections harder to treat.
Antibiotics are medicines that treat bacterial infections. They are not effective against viral infections such as colds and influenza, and taking them unnecessarily contributes to resistance.
Tobacco use is a leading cause of preventable death. It causes cancers, heart disease and lung disease, and exposure to second-hand smoke also harms people who do not smoke.
Seasonal influenza is an acute respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses. Annual vaccination is the most effective way to prevent severe illness, and antibiotics do not treat it.
Measles is a highly contagious viral disease that spreads through the air. It can be prevented with two doses of a safe and effective vaccine.

HIV attacks the immune system. It is transmitted through blood, certain body fluids and from mother to child, and it is not spread by everyday contact such as hugging, shaking hands or sharing a toilet.
Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites that are spread to people through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes. It is preventable and curable.

Diabetes is a chronic disease that occurs when the pancreas does not make enough insulin or the body cannot use insulin effectively. Type 2 diabetes is strongly linked to overweight and physical inactivity.
Cancer is a leading cause of death worldwide. Many cancers can be cured if they are detected early and treated properly, and tobacco use is the single largest risk factor.
After much research, no adverse health effect has been causally linked to exposure to wireless technologies at the levels used by mobile networks. Radio waves from 5G do not spread viruses.
COVID-19 is an infectious disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Most infected people have mild to moderate illness, and vaccines lower the risk of severe disease and death.

An infodemic is an overabundance of information, including false or misleading information, that spreads during a disease outbreak. It can make it harder for people to find trustworthy guidance and can lead to risky health behaviour.

Polio is a highly infectious viral disease that mainly affects young children and can cause paralysis. There is no cure, but it is preventable with vaccination, and cases have fallen by more than 99 percent since 1988.

Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis and spreads through the air when people with active lung disease cough or sneeze. It is treatable and curable with a course of antibiotics.

passages.source_title: Dengue and severe dengue fact sheet
passages.passage: Dengue is a viral infection transmitted to people through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes. It does not spread directly from person to person.

passages.source_title: Climate change and health fact sheet
passages.passage: Climate change affects human health through more frequent heatwaves and extreme weather, air pollution, changes in the spread of infectious diseases, and pressure on food and water supplies.

Earth's global average temperature has risen since the late 19th century, and the most recent decade is among the warmest on record. Several independent measurement records agree on this long-term warming.

Human activities, mainly the burning of coal, oil and gas, have increased the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. Scientific assessments conclude that this is the dominant cause of warming observed since the mid-20th century.

Atmospheric carbon dioxide has been measured continuously at Mauna Loa Observatory since 1958. Concentrations have risen steadily and are now far above the pre-industrial level of about 280 parts per million.
Global mean sea level is rising because ocean water expands as it warms and because ice sheets and glaciers on land are melting and adding water to the ocean.

The Antarctic ozone hole was caused by man-made chlorine and bromine compounds such as chlorofluorocarbons. International controls on these chemicals have allowed the ozone layer to begin slowly recovering.
Apollo 11 landed the first humans on the Moon on July 20, 1969. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the lunar surface while Michael Collins remained in orbit in the command module.
The Moon orbits Earth roughly once every 27 days and is the only place beyond Earth where humans have walked. It has no substantial atmosphere and its surface is covered in craters.
Ocean tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon, with a smaller contribution from the Sun, acting on Earth's oceans as the planet rotates.
The Sun is a star at the centre of our solar system, about 150 million kilometres from Earth. Its light takes roughly eight minutes to reach us.

passages.source_title: NASA Space Place: What causes the seasons?
passages.passage: Earth has seasons because its rotation axis is tilted by about 23.5 degrees relative to its orbit around the Sun. Seasons are not caused by Earth being closer to or farther from the Sun.
A black hole is a region of space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape once it crosses the boundary known as the event horizon.
Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and has a thin atmosphere made mostly of carbon dioxide. Robotic missions are studying it, and life has not been confirmed there.
Earth is the third planet from the Sun, and about 70 percent of its surface is covered by water. It is the only planet known to support life.
Earth is about 4.54 billion years old, an age established by radiometric dating of meteorites and the oldest rocks and minerals.

passages.source_title: CODATA value: speed of light in vacuum
passages.passage: The speed of light in a vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second. This value is fixed by the international definition of the metre.
The Human Genome Project produced the first reference sequence of human DNA, which contains about three billion base pairs. The project was declared complete in 2003.
The United Nations estimated that the world population reached eight billion people in November 2022.

Hypertension, or high blood pressure, is a major risk factor for heart disease, stroke and kidney disease. It often causes no symptoms, so measuring blood pressure is the only way to know, and it can be controlled with less salt, regular physical activity and medicines.

Overweight and obesity mean abnormal or excessive fat accumulation that raises the risk of type 2 diabetes, heart disease and some cancers. It results from a long-term imbalance between energy eaten and energy used, shaped by diet, physical activity and the surrounding environment.

Depression is a common mental disorder marked by persistent low mood or loss of interest in activities. It is not a sign of weakness, and effective treatments exist, including psychological therapies and, for some people, antidepressant medication.

Road traffic crashes are a leading cause of death and injury, especially among children and young adults. Seat belts, helmets, sensible speed limits and avoiding drink-driving all reduce deaths and serious injuries.

Regular physical activity lowers the risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes and some cancers and benefits mental health. WHO recommends that adults do at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity physical activity each week.

A healthy diet includes plenty of fruit, vegetables, legumes, nuts and whole grains, and limits free sugars, salt and saturated fats. Eating well throughout life helps protect against malnutrition and noncommunicable diseases such as diabetes and heart disease.

WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months of life, followed by continued breastfeeding alongside nutritious complementary foods. Breast milk supplies the nutrients infants need and helps protect them against common childhood illnesses.
Hepatitis B is a viral infection that attacks the liver and can become chronic, leading to cirrhosis and liver cancer. A safe and effective vaccine prevents it.

Cholera is an acute diarrhoeal infection caused by eating or drinking food or water contaminated with the bacterium Vibrio cholerae. It spreads where sanitation and clean water are lacking, and prompt rehydration treatment saves lives.

Rabies is a vaccine-preventable viral disease passed to people through bites or scratches from infected animals, most often dogs. It is almost always fatal once symptoms appear, but prompt vaccination after an exposure can prevent the disease.

Ebola virus disease is a severe and often fatal illness spread through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of infected people or animals. Vaccines and treatments are available for infections caused by the Zaire ebolavirus.

passages.source_title: Human papillomavirus and cervical cancer fact sheet
passages.passage: Persistent infection with certain types of human papillomavirus causes almost all cases of cervical cancer. Vaccination against HPV, together with regular screening and treatment, can prevent most cervical cancer.
Dementia is a syndrome in which memory, thinking and behaviour decline enough to affect daily life. It is not a normal part of ageing, and Alzheimer's disease is its most common form.
Eating too much sodium raises blood pressure and the risk of heart disease and stroke. WHO recommends that adults consume less than 5 grams of salt per day.

Safe drinking water is essential for health. Contaminated water can transmit diseases such as cholera, dysentery, typhoid and polio, and many people around the world still lack safely managed drinking water.

passages.source_title: Ambient (outdoor) air quality and health fact sheet
passages.passage: Outdoor air pollution, including fine particles, contributes to heart disease, stroke, lung disease and lung cancer and causes many premature deaths worldwide. Cutting emissions from transport, energy, industry and burning of waste improves air quality.

Cardiovascular diseases, such as heart attacks and strokes, are the leading cause of death worldwide. Tobacco use, an unhealthy diet, physical inactivity and harmful use of alcohol are the main behavioural risk factors.

Mental disorders are common and affect people of every age and background. Effective prevention and treatment exist, but many people do not receive care, and stigma and discrimination are often barriers.

A stroke happens when the blood supply to part of the brain is blocked or a blood vessel in the brain bursts. High blood pressure is the most important modifiable risk factor, and fast medical treatment improves the chance of recovery.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, a gas giant made mostly of hydrogen and helium. Its Great Red Spot is a giant storm, and the planet has dozens of known moons.

Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system, hotter even than Mercury, because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat in a runaway greenhouse effect. Its surface is hot enough to melt lead.
Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. It has almost no atmosphere to hold in heat, so its surface swings between extreme heat in daylight and extreme cold at night.

A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and blocks all or part of the Sun, while a lunar eclipse happens when Earth's shadow falls on the Moon. Looking at the Sun without proper eye protection during a solar eclipse can damage your eyes.

The International Space Station is a research laboratory that orbits Earth about 400 kilometres up. Built by an international partnership, it has been continuously occupied by crews since November 2000.

The Hubble Space Telescope was launched in 1990 and orbits Earth, observing the universe in visible, ultraviolet and near-infrared light. Being above the atmosphere lets it take sharp images unaffected by atmospheric blurring.

The James Webb Space Telescope launched in December 2021 and observes mainly in infrared light. It operates about 1.5 million kilometres from Earth, near a point where the gravity of the Sun and Earth keep it in a stable position.

Asteroids are rocky remnants left over from the formation of the solar system, and most orbit in a belt between Mars and Jupiter. NASA tracks near-Earth asteroids to assess any possible impact hazard.
Comets are frozen bodies of ice, dust and rock. When one approaches the Sun, its ice vaporises and forms a glowing cloud and a tail that points away from the Sun.
Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 were launched in 1977 to study the outer planets. Both spacecraft have since crossed into interstellar space, the region beyond the influence of the Sun's solar wind.

passages.source_title: What are El Nino and La Nina?
passages.passage: El Nino and La Nina are opposite phases of a natural climate pattern in the tropical Pacific Ocean. They change weather patterns such as rainfall and temperature in many parts of the world.

passages.source_title: What is the difference between weather and climate?
passages.passage: Weather describes atmospheric conditions over a short time, such as a day or a week, while climate is the average pattern of weather in a place over many years. A single cold day therefore does not disprove long-term warming.

Ocean acidification is a fall in the pH of seawater caused mainly by the ocean absorbing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. It can harm shell-building animals such as corals, oysters and some plankton.

passages.source_title: How much of the Earth is covered by ocean?
passages.passage: The ocean covers about 71 percent of Earth's surface and holds roughly 97 percent of the planet's water.

passages.source_title: This Dynamic Earth: the story of plate tectonics
passages.passage: Earth's rigid outer shell is broken into large plates that move slowly over the planet's surface. Most earthquakes and volcanoes occur along the boundaries where these plates meet.
The Higgs boson was discovered in 2012 by the ATLAS and CMS experiments at CERN's Large Hadron Collider. It is linked to a field that gives mass to elementary particles.

Climate change refers to long-term shifts in temperatures and weather patterns. Since the 1800s, human activities, mainly the burning of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas, have been the main driver of these shifts.
